Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Dr Smith, Practice: Babylon (full address not recorded). Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (early Generalized Anxiety Disorder) – work-related onset 2 months ago
- Secondary: Emerging Depressive Symptoms (possible Major Depressive Episode, anxious distress specifier)
- Tertiary: Palpitations/Insomnia – rule out medical contributors (e.g., thyroid dysfunction, arrhythmia)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: None reported
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: None
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): None
- Family History: Mother with past depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Resides with parents
- Social Support: Good family support; avoids friends recently
- Occupation/Education: New head-office role in fashion retail (high stress; hostile supervisor)
- Alcohol Use: Binge drinking most Fri/Sat; occasional weekday wine (exceeds recommended limits)
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasional smoker; denies recreational drug use
- Key Stressors: New job demands, negative boss interactions, crowded public transport, fear of lateness

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Appeared visibly distressed/anxious on video; cooperative
- Mood & Affect: Subjective anxiety; low mood; affect congruent
- Speech & Thought: Normal rate/flow; coherent content; ruminative worry about work
- Perception: No hallucinations or delusions reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Intact (time, place, person)
- Attention/Concentration: Not recorded
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Good insight; appropriate help-seeking

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Severe onset insomnia; total sleep ≈3–4 h/night; non-restorative
- Appetite: Essentially unchanged; increased chocolate intake
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly reduced daytime energy and enjoyment
- Anxiety Symptoms: Morning palpitations (irregular, minutes), racing heart, dread, muscle tension, avoidance

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies suicidal ideation or self-harm; no risk to others
- Protective Factors: Supportive parents, intact future orientation, motivation for treatment
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
Predisposing – Family history of depression; personal tendency to worry  
Precipitating – Onset of highly stressful new job with critical supervisor 2 months ago  
Perpetuating – Continued workplace stress, poor sleep, alcohol binges, avoidance of pleasurable activities, physiological arousal (palpitations)  
Protective – Supportive family, willingness to engage in therapy, intact insight

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related anxiety/adjustment disorder
- Patient Goal(s): Feel calmer before work; sleep >6 h/night; manage palpitations
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce GAD-7–consistent symptoms by ≥50% within 3 months; restore functional ability and sleep hygiene
- Actions (Patient): Self-refer to NHS talking therapies (CBT/IAPT); utilise online CBT resources provided; practise daily relaxation/breathing; monitor sleep and anxiety triggers; limit alcohol intake
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide self-referral link and written resources (anxiety management, sleep hygiene); order basic blood panel including FBC, TSH, electrolytes; arrange follow-up phone/GP review 1 week post-bloods; consider pharmacotherapy if no improvement or worsening

Secondary Problem: Low mood/anhedonia
- Patient Goal(s): Regain enjoyment in running/tennis; reconnect with friends weekly
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor mood (e.g., PHQ-9); prevent progression to major depressive episode
- Actions (Patient): Schedule at least one pleasurable or social activity per week; maintain mood diary; exercise gradually
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Screen with PHQ-9 at follow-up; reinforce behavioural activation; consider referral to counselling/psychology if depressive symptoms escalate; discuss medication options if criteria met

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: anxiety physiology, CBT techniques, sleep hygiene, alcohol effects, self-referral pathway
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Further sleep reduction, daily palpitations, inability to attend work, increasing social withdrawal
- Coping Strategies: Breathing/relaxation exercises, graded exposure to feared situations, maintaining routine, reduced alcohol, seeking support from family/friends

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: NHS IAPT/talking therapies (awaiting self-referral)
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: 1 week after blood results (then 4–6 weeks to review therapy progress)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (High) – Clear temporal link to new job; pervasive worry, somatic tension, sleep disturbance
- Major Depressive Disorder, anxious distress specifier (Medium) – Low mood, anhedonia, fatigue; monitor progression
- Hyperthyroidism (Low–Medium) – Palpitations and anxiety could be thyrotoxic; screening bloods ordered

Quality checks

● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx  
● Transcript quality notes: Good audio; no vital signs or objective tests available
